dropped_non_competitor.name: SSL4EO
dropped_non_competitor.reason: the numbers are real, the model is not recoverable. Thirteen of these seventeen results are one number trail: SelectiveMAE states its AID/RESISC-45/DIOR values are “taken directly from SkySense”, RS-vHeat follows “the configurations of RingMo and SkySense”, and DOFA carries one of the same values. SkySense — where the trail ends — has no backbone column, never names the pretraining method, and mentions SSL4EO nowhere but in its tables. The four papers that added a backbone afterwards disagree for identical scores: RS-vHeat prints ResNet-50 (24M), SelectiveMAE and the MIMRS survey print ViT-S (22M), and DOFA prints ViT-B, which SSL4EO-S12 never released. ResNet-50 admits MoCo-v2 and DINO; ViT-S admits MAE, MoCo-v3, DINO and data2vec — between them all six released checkpoints, so there is no defensible row to put these on

The paper promises "will be released at: https://github.com/1921134176/CGEarthEye" and the corpus recorded code and weights as available on that basis. The repository returns 404 and a GitHub search for CGEarthEye finds nothing, so the promise is unkept as of today. Note that arXiv's HTML route serves an abstract page rather than a full text for this paper; the quote is read from the PDF. Compute added 2026-10-29: "The experiment was conducted over 150 days using 16 NVIDIA A800 GPUs (80GB)", corroborated by the hardware table, "GPU: 16x NVIDIA A800 GPU / 80GB VRAM". What makes it worth recording is that it is wrong. SkySense's own paper says it was "distributed over 80 A100-80GB GPUs" — 80 GPUs, not 80 servers of eight — so CGEarthEye overstates a competitor's training cost by a factor of eight in the course of arguing that its own is lower. A2-MAE quotes the same figure correctly as "80 A100 GPUs".
